title: Length bound for multiplication witnesses
statement: Let $z$ and $S$ be bit strings, and let $u$ and $v$ be the total first and second projections of $z$. Suppose there are bit strings $A,B,C$ such that $S$ encodes the pair $(A,	ext{the pair }(B,C))$, the value of $C$ plus the product of the values of $A$ and $B$ equals the product of the values of $u$ and $v$, $C$ is the canonical bit representation of its value, and $|A|+|B|\le |u|+|v|$. Then $|S|\le 4(|z|+1)$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes bit-string length and the value of a bit string is its little-endian binary value.
hypotheses_covered: Existence of bit strings $A,B,C$ with the specified nested encoding of $S$
$C$ is the canonical bit representation of its value
